question: Which architecture should task #196's implement phase build for translation (S4) verification?
answer: APPROVED: Two-axis differential. Extend test_formula.py::TestTranslateTruthPreservation to cover the box half. Required design properties, all user-approved and binding on implementation: (1) ORACLE INDEPENDENCE -- the reference evaluator must NOT route through translate(), or the test is circular and passes under the very bug it targets; preserve the existing test's independent-evaluation design. (2) TWO AXES -- GENERATE small-depth sentences covering every defined operator (negation, conjunction, disjunction, derived tense operators, \next, \prev) so elimination coverage is broad, and HAND-BUILD the label families so the box dimension has genuine multi-lasso structure; reuse tests/fixtures/certificates/01_positive_box.json and 03_box_unfaithful.json plus the independent decoder in test_certificate_fixtures.py rather than inventing new infrastructure. (3) ASYMMETRIC UNTIL/SINCE IS MANDATORY -- generated Until/Since cases MUST include instances where event and guard are genuinely distinguishable and swapping them changes the truth value at some point in the model. The guard/event swap hazard is invisible on the wire (named fields are order-free), so the differential is the only place it can surface, and only asymmetric cases are sensitive to it. Operator coverage is NOT hazard sensitivity. (4) BOX COVERAGE EXPLICIT -- oracle/bimodal_logic/ground_truth.py covers only the five primitive tense tags with no box case, so the box half cannot be inherited from it and must be covered directly. (5) Record Route 1 (relocate elimination into verified code) as INFEASIBLE with its reason -- translate() runs at Python evaluation time inside every primitive operator's true_at, not just at export, and Lean has no callable verified elimination pass to relocate into -- and record the Lean-side translation cross-check as DEFERRED (counterpart confirmed absent from the local BimodalLogic checkout). REJECTED alternatives and why: round-trip inverse check (verifies structure not truth preservation; a symmetric bug in both directions cancels invisibly); hand-built cases only (coverage limited to what someone thought to write down); deferring to the Lean counterpart (leaves the weakest joint unverified indefinitely on unscoped external work).

question: Should ModelChecker be refactored so Until/Since argument order matches the Lean development throughout?
answer: APPROVED AND REQUIRED, user-directed: normalize ModelChecker to GUARD-FIRST, matching Lean's untl/snce, so that translate() no longer swaps and a reader working in both repositories sees ONE argument order. This is a scope ADDITION to task 196 and must be planned as phases that run BEFORE the verification phases, since the tests must be written against the normalized convention rather than the current one. Rationale: guard-first matches both Lean and the mainstream LTL reading of A U B (A holds until B happens); the existing event-first order cites the Burgess convention, and that citation is deliberately dropped in favor of cross-repository uniformity. SITES THAT MUST ALL MOVE TOGETHER (grep-confirmed, 91 occurrences across .py files plus docs): (1) operators.py -- UntilOperator.true_at/false_at and SinceOperator.true_at/false_at parameter order and every docstring describing the order, including the Burgess-convention paragraph and the Key Properties/Example blocks; (2) semantic/formula.py -- translate's \Until and \Since rules become positional-identity (Untl(guard=translate(arguments[0]), event=translate(arguments[1]))), and the module docstring section titled "The Until/Since guard/event swap" must be rewritten to record that there is no longer a swap; (3) oracle/bimodal_logic/translation.py:60-61 -- the mapping "untl": ("\\Until", "event", "guard") and its snce counterpart encode the event-first order for the oracle's JSON-to-infix direction and MUST be flipped in lockstep, or the brute-force adjudicator silently disagrees with the theory; (4) EVERY \Until / \Since formula STRING in examples.py, README.md, docs/API_REFERENCE.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, and the test files test_until_since_integration.py, test_certificate_a2_triangle.py, test_structure.py, test_operators.py, test_proposition.py, test_next_prev.py, test_formula.py, oracle/bimodal_logic/tests/test_json_translation.py, oracle/bimodal_logic/tests/test_oracle_interface.py. CRITICAL HAZARD: this is a SEMANTIC change, not a rename. Every existing two-argument \Until/\Since occurrence must have its arguments swapped, or that formula silently changes meaning and any test asserting its truth value will either break loudly (good) or, worse, keep passing while asserting something different. Each occurrence must be inspected and flipped deliberately; a blind sed is forbidden. Expected signal: a phase that flips operators.py and translate() WITHOUT flipping the formula strings should turn the suite red, and that red should be used as the checklist of order-sensitive sites rather than avoided. CONSEQUENCE FOR VERIFICATION: once normalized there is no swap left for the differential test to catch, so the asymmetric Until/Since requirement recorded in the previous decision is retained for a different reason -- general truth preservation across the event/guard distinction -- and NOT dropped. SEQUENCING: land after tasks 193 and 194 (both touch the same bimodal test tree, and 193 adds closure formulas to test_certificate_a2_triangle.py), and sweep any \Until/\Since occurrences those tasks introduce. VERIFY: full bimodal suite, the oracle suite, and the four-theory gate; every previously-passing truth-value assertion must still pass after both the convention and its formula strings are flipped together.
